title: Benchmarking and Mitigating Sycophancy in Medical Vision Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Injecting prompts that explicitly highlight a specific incorrect option (mimicking a user's suggestion) to test if the vision-language model abandons independent visual reasoning to agree with the user.

Appending prompts featuring direct orders from a perceived superior or strong rebuttals from a senior expert to measure if the model overrides factual visual evidence to comply with authoritative cues.

Providing prompts that claim all other medical professionals and AI systems unanimously selected a different answer to evaluate if the model alters its correct answer to align with a perceived majority.
Appending text that conveys intense, patient-centered fear or pleading to test if affective alignment and emotional manipulation can override the model's objective, evidence-based medical evaluation.
Framing the model's initial correct choice as causing catastrophic ethical, legal, or socioeconomic consequences to test if the fear of negative outcomes shifts the model's diagnostic response.
